properties.chose: Anthony kept (a), (b) and (c) on 2026-10-10. (b) is req:two-or-more-designs-are-compared-on-one-topic-on-demand and (c) is req:a-composed-analysis-across-a-familys-designs-writes-its-seam-gaps-back-to-the-hub, both reflow2's; (a) widened flo2's req:flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-graph-when-asked from a hub's designs to any set the person may read. (d), the by-hand comparison through two connections, stays what works today. His further idea, a design taking a chunk of another, is its own open question: dec:idea-a-design-takes-a-chunk-of-another-design-and-inherits-it.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-10, dev_reflow2 hub session, after choosing "assembled when asked" over a stored union: "'assembled when asked' would really make queries across multiple hubs very efficient and exhaustive. It might even lead to gap discovery where two designs don't 'interface' properly. Secondly, I've done it on other occasions, but today I asked the storyflow project to reference the oauth implementation in flo2 (via the connector). As both are my designs, could you rapidly 'assemble' flo2 + storyflow or since this was a comparison operation, would it be more a 'oauth 2 keys:values' in flo2 <-compared-> 'oauth 2 keys:values' in storyflow? I'd imagine these types of operations at the key:value level could be done very rapidly and on demand?"

WHAT EXISTS, so the question is narrower than it sounds:
- WHOLE-DESIGN ASSEMBLY: compose_and_analyse (req:composed-analysis) imports one design into another under a namespace and runs the ordinary checks over the whole, so a seam's faults surface as the gaps they already are: a contract with no provider once both sides are present, a requirement nothing satisfies across the join, one thing named twice. That IS his "two designs don't interface properly" finder. It opens designs by path, so flo2.io withholds it; the hosted half is flo2's req:flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-graph-when-asked (accepted today, scoped to a hub's designs).
- SEAMS: cap:seam-incompatibility says when two linked designs disagree at a boundary; cap:complementary-pairing computes the seam by role; both need a declared Interface on each side, which flo2 and StoryFlow do not have for OAuth.
- TOPICS: topic_report gathers one design's nodes around a topic, in one design only. No comparison of a topic across two designs exists.
- WHAT THE STORYFLOW SESSION DID TODAY: read flo2's OAuth nodes one by one through the connector and rewrote them as StoryFlow requirements with prose citations (now typed links). An assembled, topic-scoped read would have handed it both sides at once.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) WIDEN ASSEMBLY FROM "A HUB'S DESIGNS" TO "ANY SET THE PERSON MAY READ": compose N named designs for one question, hub or not. On flo2.io, a flo2 change to the accepted requirement's scope; locally, compose_and_analyse already takes any two by path. SMALL on the reflow2 side (none), SMALL on flo2's (a parameter listing designs).
(b) A TOPIC-SCOPED COMPARE: `compare_topic` (or topic_report with `designs`): for a topic, take each design's topic neighbourhood (search hits plus their edges, as topic_report does), assemble them under namespaces, and report side by side: what one holds and the other lacks, requirements whose statements match closely (the family check's similarity sweep, at a stated threshold), interfaces or constraints that disagree, and what neither declares. The agent then judges. MEDIUM: a reflow2 tool built from topic_report + compose + the duplicate guard's scoring; cheap to run because it never opens more than the two neighbourhoods.
(c) SEAM GAPS FROM ASSEMBLY, SERVED: a composed analysis across a hub's members whose findings are written back as cross-design gaps (relation unstated, interface declared on one side only, requirement sent down and never accepted) so a hub's loop_status shows them. MEDIUM, on both sides: reflow2 names the finding kinds; the host runs it on a schedule or on ask.
(d) AS TODAY: the agent reads both designs through two connections and compares in its own context. Zero cost; what the StoryFlow session did, slowly and by hand.

PUSHBACK, KEPT BESIDE IT:
- "RAPIDLY" IS BOUNDED BY OPENING, NOT BY SCANNING. A key:value scan is microseconds; opening a design is 0.3 s for a small one and 8 to 11 s for reflow2's own (measured today). Topic scoping (b) wins by opening less, not by comparing faster.
- KEY:VALUE EQUALITY FINDS LITTLE ACROSS DESIGNS WRITTEN IN DIFFERENT WORDS. The family check measured a similarity sweep at 0.4 finding a true duplicate one time in eight (fact:the-dev-reflow2-family-holds-five-facts-twice-...-2026-10-09). A comparison at the key:value level is a candidate generator; the judgement that flo2's audience check and StoryFlow's are "the same thing" stays the agent's or the person's. (b) must say so in its reply.
- GAP DISCOVERY AT A SEAM NEEDS A DECLARED SEAM. compose_and_analyse finds a contract with no provider only where an Interface is declared; two designs that never declared how they meet produce no seam gap, only "nothing links them", which is the members_unlinked finding loop_status already gives.
- PERMISSIONS AND COST: assembly reads N stores on the shared box (the capacity road); an answer must leave out a design the caller cannot read and say so. With hub membership cascading (flo2's req:membership-of-a-hub-grants-reach-into-every-design-it-names) the "may read" set is the hub's, which makes (a) cheap to state.
- HIS OWN WORD EARLIER TODAY: StoryFlow and flo2 are NOT to be connected (no pin). (a) and (b) need no pin: they are a question, not a link.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-10 — designs are compared on one topic on demand (b), any set the person may read is assembled, hub or not (a), and a composed analysis writes its seam gaps back to the hub (c); by hand through two connections stays considered
